content: The dosage of this medication is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also calculated based on their weight. It is important to note that different brands of this medication may deliver varying amounts of the active ingredient. To achieve the maximum benefit, use this medication consistently as prescribed. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, or joint and muscle pain. Occasionally, you may notice whole or partially intact tablets or capsules in your stool. If this happens frequently, inform your doctor. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, mesalamine may exacerbate ulcerative colitis. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are uncommon but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar concerns. Before starting mesalamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminosalicylates (e.g., balsalazide, olsalazine), salicylates (e.g., aspirin, salsalate), sulfasalazine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, particularly if you have pre-existing skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis or eczema. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication is chemically similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years of age should not take aspirin or aspirin-related medications (e.g., salicylates) if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine, due to the risk of Reye’s syndrome. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Mesalamine is closely related to balsalazide, olsalazine, and sulfasalazine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels), potentially leading to false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver and kidney function) may be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during treatment to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If your medication bottle contains a desiccant, keep it in the bottle to protect the medication from moisture. Ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
